clue.text: Suit and tie

definitions.meaning: to suit is to go well with, to correspond
a tie is a sporting fixture, as in a cup tie

explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a cup tie is a knockout game, so 'tie' is a game rather than neckwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: to go with something is to suit it, and a sporting fixture is a game between two sides.

clue.text: With therapeutic properties claimed in error

indicators.note: in error suggests the letters are wrongly placed and need sorting

explanation.surface: Some product is said to have healing benefits, a claim that is false.
explanation.definitionFit: Something healing or curative has properties used to treat illness.

clue.text: Watch brief uprising

indicators.note: in a down clue, uprising means the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a remit is a brief or terms of reference

explanation.surface: A short account of a rebellion is observed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' reverses REMIT in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopwatch or clock that counts down is a timing device, like a watch.

clue.text: The morning after George's beginning to move into his house …

indicators.note: says that letter is placed inside the royal house

parts.note: the House of Hanover was the royal family of the four King Georges

indicators.note: beginning picks out the first letter of George

explanation.surface: The day after a party, King George starts to take up residence at home.
explanation.walkthrough: The Georges I to IV were of the House of Hanover, so 'his house' is HANOVER; G goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangover is the headache and nausea felt the morning after heavy drinking.

clue.text: High-flown missile — a collection of such is incomplete

parts.note: a bomb is a missile dropped or thrown

indicators.note: incomplete says the word for the collection loses its final letter

parts.note: a stick is a set of bombs released in a row from an aircraft

explanation.surface: A missile is described as pompous, while a set of them is said to fall short.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'stick' of bombs is the run dropped together; 'is incomplete' docks its last letter to leave STIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Bombastic language is inflated and pompous, the same as high-flown rhetoric.

clue.text: … King boards large vessel

indicators.note: to board is to get on, so the king goes inside the word for large

parts.note: big means large
R is short for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch climbs aboard a great ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A brig is a two-masted sailing ship, so it is a vessel.

clue.text: Field-Marshal's capital

definitions.meaning: Bernard ..., the British field marshal of the Second World War
the capital city of the US state of Alabama

explanation.definitionFit: Monty the British commander of El Alamein shares his surname with Alabama's state capital city.

clue.text: Member of relay team secure in position

definitions.meaning: the final, usually fastest, runner or swimmer in a relay
to fix something firmly in place

explanation.definitionFit: The last leg of a relay is run by a team's strongest member, and to fix firmly in place is to make fast.

clue.text: Medical practitioner cut up, being taken in by this trick at first

indicators.note: says the reversed cut goes inside the other letters
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to pare is to cut or trim

indicators.note: picks out the opening letter of trick

explanation.surface: A doctor is upset, having been fooled by a trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medical practitioner cut up' reads as an upset doctor, but 'up' is a reversal signal, giving ERAP, and 'cut' is the synonym being reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A therapist treats patients for illness or disability, a type of medical worker.

clue.text: Acted out junior role

indicators.note: out signals the letters are rearranged, as in out of order

explanation.surface: An actor played a minor part.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadet is a trainee in the forces or police, a junior position below the officers.

clue.text: Vague rumour going around about new measure

parts.note: dim means vague or hazy

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the abbreviation is placed inside
going around turns the word for rumour back to front

parts.note: noise can mean talk or rumour going about

explanation.surface: An indistinct rumour circulates about some new policy measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going around' reverses NOISE to ESION, and 'about' puts N inside it to give ENSION.
explanation.definitionFit: A dimension is a measurement such as length or breadth, so it is a measure.

clue.text: Long, boring speech initially put out statement of belief

indicators.note: says the opening letter of the speech word is removed

parts.note: a screed is a long tedious piece of writing or speech

explanation.surface: A tedious oration was first delivered as a manifesto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially put out' removes the first letter, the S of SCREED.
explanation.definitionFit: A creed is a formal set of religious or other convictions, a statement of faith.

clue.text: Large bottle lad's added to heap

indicators.note: the boy goes after the car, joined to the end of it

parts.note: a heap is slang for a battered old car
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy's contribution is put on a pile of rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heap' is slang for an old rattletrap car, not a pile.
explanation.definitionFit: A carboy is a big glass or plastic container, often cased, for holding corrosive liquids.

clue.text: I have to admit having entered a number without a clue

indicators.note: says the number is put inside the word for admit

parts.note: to grant is to admit or concede

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to having keyed in a figure without knowing what they were doing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without a clue' is the colloquial sense of knowing nothing, not a reference to the crossword.
explanation.definitionFit: Being clueless is being uninformed, lacking knowledge of something.

clue.text: Means to form attachment — not at 18? — involving affection

indicators.note: involving means containing, so the shortened word goes round affection
not says the following word is removed from the cross-referenced answer

parts.note: the answer at 18 down
taken as written
love is affection

explanation.surface: A knot used to tie up is said not to be gossip but affection.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference with 'not at' leaves CHITCH, which 'involving' wraps round affection; the question mark flags the odd reference inside the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A clove hitch is a knot used to fasten a rope to a post, so a means of attaching.

clue.text: False name — it's not unknown in unemployed male, wanting a shift

indicators.note: wanting a shift says the letters need to be rearranged

parts.note: Y is a standard algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A jobless man looks for a work shift under an assumed identity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's not unknown in' says that the letters of UNEMPLOYED plus M contain a Y that is left out; the rest are shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen name is an assumed name used by a writer, a pseudonym.

clue.text: Temporary seamstress might

definitions.meaning: a dressmaker might sew a shift, a simple loose dress

explanation.definitionFit: An improvised stopgap is a short-term substitute, and a needlewoman could sew a loose dress.

clue.text: One wearing a decoration, a circular object

indicators.note: one wearing something has it on the outside, so the decoration goes round the numeral

parts.note: the DSC, Distinguished Service Cross, is a military decoration
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A soldier with a medal is likened to a round thing.
explanation.walkthrough: The DSC (Distinguished Service Cross) is a British military medal.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc is any flat round shape, such as a record or a plate.

clue.text: Protection against piracy — though not a piracy Goth exercised

indicators.note: exercised means worked over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Legal protection against plunder, though a Goth pirate was busy all the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'though not a' says the letters of PIRACY GOTH lose an A before being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Copyright is the legal right protecting creative work against unauthorised copying, known as piracy.

clue.text: Gossip from young girl, a spiteful female, about husband

parts.note: a chit is a cheeky young girl

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the woman goes round husband

parts.note: a cat is a spiteful woman

explanation.surface: Tittle-tattle from a girl and a catty woman concerning someone's husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Chitchat is idle chatter or small talk, the same as gossip.

clue.text: Physician nips head off liver parasite

indicators.note: says the parasite's first letter is removed

parts.note: the liver fluke is a flatworm parasite of sheep and cattle

explanation.surface: A doctor removes the head of a parasite from the liver.
explanation.walkthrough: St Luke is called 'the beloved physician' in the New Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Luke the evangelist was by tradition a doctor, named the beloved physician by Paul.

clue.text: After renaissance, poet throve inordinately

indicators.note: a renaissance is a rebirth, so the letters are reborn in a new order

explanation.surface: Following a revival, a poet flourished beyond all measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something to excess, past all reasonable limits, is going too far, an idiom from trench warfare.

clue.text: Stop Scandinavian talking

indicators.note: talking says the word is spoken, so it sounds like another

parts.note: Finnish refers to Finland, a Nordic country

explanation.surface: Ask a Norwegian to stop chattering.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish is to stop or end an activity.

clue.text: State with inadequate illumination

parts.note: GA is the abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
slight means small, insufficient

explanation.surface: A region is described as poorly lit.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaslight is lighting produced by burning gas, a form of lighting.

clue.text: Good pop music, number one in hit chart

parts.note: rap is a form of popular music

indicators.note: number one picks out the first letter of hit

explanation.surface: A great pop song tops the charts.
explanation.definitionFit: A graph is a diagram showing data, a type of chart.

clue.text: Writer who added fuel to the flames?

definitions.meaning: Bram ..., the Irish novelist who wrote Dracula

definitions.text: who added fuel to the flames?
definitions.meaning: a person who feeds a furnace or boiler with coal

explanation.definitionFit: Bram Stoker was the author of Dracula, and a ship's or engine's fireman shovels coal into a fire.

clue.text: Element I discovered in Danish bread

parts.note: Kr is the chemical symbol for the element krypton
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Some chemical is found in Danish loaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bread' is slang for money; 'discovered in' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: The krone is the currency of Denmark, and bread is slang for money.

clue.text: System of weights introduced by French sergeant

definitions.text: System of weights introduced by French
definitions.meaning: ... weight, used for precious metals, named after the French town ...
Sergeant ..., the dashing soldier in Hardy's Far From the Madding Crowd

explanation.definitionFit: The troy system measures gold and silver and takes its name from Troyes, and Hardy's seducing soldier is Sergeant Troy.

clue.text: A politician, I can offer a valid defence against most charges

definitions.text: a valid defence against most charges

parts.note: LIB is short for a Liberal, a politician

explanation.surface: A politician boasts of having a sound defence against nearly any accusation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can offer' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is proof of being elsewhere when a crime occurred, which clears a suspect of most offences.

clue.text: Expression of unrequited love — necklace and good food rejected

parts.note: a torc is a twisted metal neck ring worn by ancient Celts

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the letters of good and food together are read backwards

parts.note: nosh is slang for food

explanation.surface: A jilted lover's present of jewellery and a nice meal are turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' reverses GNOSH to HSONG after TORC.
explanation.definitionFit: A torch song is a sentimental ballad lamenting love that is not returned.

clue.text: Lambaste article written by grass (retired)

indicators.note: written by means placed next to, so the grass word follows

parts.note: to lambaste is to hit or attack
THE is the definite article
hay is dried grass

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a piece written by an informer who has since retired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' looks like British slang for an informer, but here it is dried grass.
explanation.definitionFit: To go to bed is the idiomatic meaning, and retired is an old-fashioned way of saying went to bed.

clue.text: Delightful surprise for doctor

definitions.meaning: an unexpected pleasure or special outing
to doctor is to give medical care to a patient

explanation.definitionFit: An unexpected pleasure is a delight, and to give medical care to a patient is to attend to them.
